notes.printed: Length sweep: q is a model's per-step accuracy, the share of all its pieces right pooled over the sweep's lengths (4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 steps), and q to the power N is the reference for a chain of N steps. The length sweep's by-length rows here are all Opus-medium's, and the inputs of q are its pieces per-step rows (keys ending per_step.nx1), here at 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 steps under both marking rules, each over that length's puzzles; the mark (q's input) in a row's name is the first version's own wording, so only its rows carry it (the rows added by rule are named by their family, model, measure, length and shape, and their keys show which are inputs of q); Opus-medium's q itself, pooled over every length, has a zero-width stamped interval under each rule and no exact interval (the scope note gives free analysis 4's reason), while the other models' q intervals have width.
raw: the length sweep's q is estimated from pieces only, so its exact counterpart is the pieces per-step row
curve: q pools every piece-step over all lengths and sets (clusters stratified by set), so no single count of base puzzles carries it, and its q^N bands are powers of its interval; no exact interval

each stamped interval keeps its source's label, given in its own column: the source's stamped label (for Study 1b's descriptive blocks, the block's name; for the length sweep, its stamped plan line; for the Pilot 1 markers the length-sweep files carry, exploratory, the label the plan gives Pilot 1's 24-step markers (they ran before Lock 2, with a different rule mix, sets and timing); for free analysis 2, its stamped label), or, where the source stamps none, the plan's label for the output that reports it (FIG-02 for item 20; TAB-11 for Study 1b's per-test cells). Samples per puzzle: a vote row gives its k, the samples it votes over; a row with several single samples averages over them; either way the puzzle counts once in the count of puzzles right; a Pilot 1 marker's samples are not stamped in the length-sweep files.

Names: Item 7 is a Study 1 reporting item, per-piece accuracy: the share of a sample's pieces that are right, averaged over the puzzle's designed samples and then over puzzles; Item 9e is a Study 1 reporting item, the offline escalate-to-Opus cascade: its key ends in the number of Haiku-medium samples in the cascade's vote (k_c) and then even, the even-indexed puzzles, where the cascade is scored; Opus-medium's accuracy there is one estimate, the same for every k_c, so these rows repeat it; C10 is the keep-list analysis of the paired difference in single-sample accuracy between two effort levels of one model; a vote of k samples scores one answer per puzzle from those samples; a vote-curve point is the vote at one k; 'pooled' in a row name or key means both shapes together, each puzzle counted once, not pooled over lengths; 'chains' is the chain shape.
